item.title: Chicago’s Newberry Library gets $4 million to help tribal nations revitalize Indigenous languages
item.description: <p>Chicago’s Newberry Library has received $4 million from the Mellon Foundation that will help widen access to Indigenous languages, some of which have been on the brink of disappearance.</p><p>The research library holds roughly 2,400 items directly related to more than 300 different Indigenous languages as part of its vast Indigenous Studies collections, which include more than one million manuscript pages, 11,000 photographs and 2,000 maps.</p><p>Right now, only a small percentage of that is

item.title: How Jesse Jackson shaped Chicago education, from protesting school segregation to reopening Dyett HS
item.description: <p>When the Rev. Jesse Jackson arrived in Chicago in 1964, he came face to face with a segregated school system where Black and Latino students attempted to learn in schools so overcrowded that hallways became classrooms and supplies were scarce. He quickly jumped into the fight to end disparities in education — a cause he’d champion throughout his life.</p><p>Early on, he helped organize protests against the poor learning conditions. item.title: Definition Theatre's 'Black Cypress Bayou' centers a Black matriarch with secrets
item.description: <p>My great grandmother was born and raised in central Texas. She lived into her late 90s. She had an elementary school education, due to dropping out to help the family work in the fields. She lived half her life a stones-throw away from the plantation her elders had been enslaved on before moving with her daughter to the West Coast.</p><p>One of my most vivid memories of my great grandmother is her singing.
